text: Let $(2,3)$ be the largest open interval in which the function $f(x)=2\log _{\mathrm{e}}(x-2)-x^{2}+ax+1$ is strictly increasing and (b, c) be the largest open interval, in which the function $\mathrm{g}(x)=(x-1)^{3}(x+2-\mathrm{a})^{2}$ is strictly decreasing. Then $100(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{c})$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=2\ln (x-2)-x^{2}+ax+1$ is defined for $x>2$, and

$f^{'}(x)=\dfrac{2}{x-2}-2x+a,f^{''}(x)=-\dfrac{2}{(x-2)^{2}}-2<0$

So $f^{'}$ is strictly decreasing on $(2,\infty )$, with $f^{'}(x)\to \infty$ as $x\to 2^{+}$. Hence $f^{'}>0$ exactly on $(2,x_{0})$, where $f^{'}(x_{0})=0$, and this is the largest open interval in which $f$ is strictly increasing. As this interval is $(2,3)$, $x_{0}=3$:

$f^{'}(3)=2-6+a=0\Rightarrow a=4$

Then $g(x)=(x-1)^{3}(x-2)^{2}$ and

$g^{'}(x)=3(x-1)^{2}(x-2)^{2}+2(x-1)^{3}(x-2)=(x-1)^{2}(x-2)(5x-8)$

Since $(x-1)^{2}\geq 0$, $g^{'}(x)<0$ exactly when $(x-2)(5x-8)<0$, i.e. $\dfrac{8}{5}<x<2$. So $(b,c)=\left (\dfrac{8}{5},2\right )$.

$100(a+b-c)=100\left (4+\dfrac{8}{5}-2\right )=360$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\left \{x\in (0,π)-\left \{\frac{π}{2}\right \}:\log _{(2/π)}|\sin x|+\log _{(2/π)}|\cos x|=2\right \}$ and $\mathrm{B}=\{x⩾0:\sqrt{x}(\sqrt{x}-4)-3|\sqrt{x}-2|+6=0\}$. Then $\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{A}\cup \mathrm{B})$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For A, both logarithms are defined on $(0,π)-\left \{\dfrac{π}{2}\right \}$, and adding them:

$\log _{2/π}|\sin x\cos x|=2\Rightarrow |\sin x\cos x|=\dfrac{4}{π^{2}}\Rightarrow |\sin 2x|=\dfrac{8}{π^{2}}$

Since $0<\dfrac{8}{π^{2}}\approx 0.81<1$ and $2x\in (0,2π)$, $\sin 2x=\dfrac{8}{π^{2}}$ gives two values of $x$ in $\left (0,\dfrac{π}{2}\right )$ and $\sin 2x=-\dfrac{8}{π^{2}}$ gives two in $\left (\dfrac{π}{2},π\right )$, so $n(A)=4$.


[IMG]

For B, put $t=\sqrt{x}\geq 0$:

$t^{2}-4t-3|t-2|+6=0$

For $0\leq t<2$, $|t-2|=2-t$, so $-3|t-2|=3t-6$:

$t^{2}-4t+3t-6+6=0\Rightarrow t(t-1)=0\Rightarrow t=0,1\Rightarrow x=0,1$

For $t\geq 2$, $|t-2|=t-2$:

$t^{2}-4t-3t+6+6=0\Rightarrow t^{2}-7t+12=0\Rightarrow t=3,4\Rightarrow x=9,16$

So $B=\{0,1,9,16\}$ and $n(B)=4$. No element of B lies in A: $0$, $9$ and $16$ are outside $(0,π)$, and $|\sin 2|\approx 0.91\neq \dfrac{8}{π^{2}}$. Therefore

$n(A\cup B)=4+4=8$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: If the equation of the parabola with vertex $\mathrm{V}\left (\frac{3}{2},3\right )$ and the directrix $x+2y=0$ is $αx^{2}+βy^{2}-γxy-30x-60y+225=0$, then $α+β+γ$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The axis passes through the vertex $V\left (\dfrac{3}{2},3\right )$ and is perpendicular to the directrix $x+2y=0$ (slope $-\dfrac{1}{2}$), so its slope is $2$:

$y-3=2\left (x-\frac{3}{2}\right )\Rightarrow y=2x$

The axis meets the directrix where $x+2(2x)=0$, i.e. at $Z(0,0)$.

The vertex is the midpoint of $Z$ and the focus $S$, so $S=\left (2\cdot \dfrac{3}{2}-0,2\cdot 3-0\right )=(3,6)$.

Every point $(x,y)$ of the parabola is equidistant from $S$ and the directrix:

$(x-3)^{2}+(y-6)^{2}=\frac{(x+2y)^{2}}{5}$

$5x^{2}+5y^{2}-30x-60y+225=x^{2}+4xy+4y^{2}$

$4x^{2}+y^{2}-4xy-30x-60y+225=0$

Comparing with $αx^{2}+βy^{2}-γxy-30x-60y+225=0$: $α=4$, $β=1$, $γ=4$, so $α+β+γ=9$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: Let the points $\left (\frac{11}{2},α\right )$ lie on or inside the triangle with sides $x+y=11,x+2y=16$ and $2x+3y=29$. Then the product of the smallest and the largest values of $α$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
The sides $L_{1}:x+y=11$, $L_{2}:x+2y=16$ and $L_{3}:2x+3y=29$ meet pairwise at

$L_{1}\cap L_{2}=(6,5),L_{1}\cap L_{3}=(4,7),L_{2}\cap L_{3}=(10,3)$

The line $x=\dfrac{11}{2}$ lies between $x=4$ and $x=10$. It crosses side $L_{1}$ (from $(4,7)$ to $(6,5)$) and side $L_{3}$ (from $(4,7)$ to $(10,3)$), but not side $L_{2}$, which spans only $6\leq x\leq 10$.

On $L_{1}$: $α=11-\dfrac{11}{2}=\dfrac{11}{2}$. On $L_{3}$: $3α=29-11=18\Rightarrow α=6$.

So $\dfrac{11}{2}\leq α\leq 6$, and the product of the smallest and largest values is $\dfrac{11}{2}\times 6=33$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: Let $[x]$ denote the greatest integer function, and let m and n respectively be the numbers of the points, where the function $f(x)=[x]+|x-2|,-2<x<3$, is not continuous and not differentiable. Then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $-2<x<3$, $[x]$ is constant between consecutive integers and $|x-2|$ changes form at $x=2$, so

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} -x, & -2<x<-1 \\ 1-x, & -1\leq x<0 \\ 2-x, & 0\leq x<1 \\ 3-x, & 1\leq x<2 \\ x, & 2\leq x<3 \end{array} \right.$

At each of $x=-1,0,1,2$ the left-hand limit is $1$ while the value of $f$ is $2$, so $f$ is discontinuous at these 4 points and $m=4$.

A function is not differentiable where it is discontinuous, so $f$ is not differentiable at these 4 points. Between them $f$ is linear, hence differentiable; the corner of $|x-2|$ at $x=2$ is already one of the 4 points. So $n=4$.

$m+n=4+4=8$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: Let $f:(0,\infty )\to 𝐑$ be a function which is differentiable at all points of its domain and satisfies the condition $x^{2}f^{'}(x)=2xf(x)+3$, with $f(1)=4$. Then $2f(2)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} x^{2}f^{'}(x)-2xf(x)=3 \\ \left (\dfrac{x^{2}f^{'}(x)-2xf(x)}{(x^{2})^{2}}\right )=\dfrac{3}{(x^{2})^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{d}{dx}\left (\dfrac{f(x)}{x^{2}}\right )=\dfrac{3}{x^{4}} \end{array}$

Integrating both sides

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{x}^{2}}=-\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{x}^{3}}+\mathrm{C} \\ \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=-\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{Cx}^{2} \\ \text{put}\mathrm{x}=1 \\ 4=-1+\mathrm{C}\Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=5 \\ \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=-\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{x}}+5\mathrm{x}^{2} \end{array}$

Now $2\times f(2)=2\times \left [-\frac{1}{2}+5\times 2^{2}\right ]$

$=39$

text: If $\int \frac{2x^{2}+5x+9}{\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}}\mathrm{d}x=x\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+α\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+β\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left |x+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}\right |+\mathrm{C}$, where $C$ is the constant of integration, then $α+2β$ is equal to $__________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Writing the numerator in terms of the radicand and its derivative:

$2x^{2}+5x+9=2(x^{2}+x+1)+\frac{3}{2}(2x+1)+\frac{11}{2}.$

So the integral equals

$2\int \sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}dx+\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}}dx+\frac{11}{2}\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}}.$

With $x^{2}+x+1=\left (x+\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}+\frac{3}{4}$ and $L=\log _{e}\left |x+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}\right |$, the standard forms give

$2\int \sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}dx=2\left [\frac{x+\frac{1}{2}}{2}\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+\frac{3}{8}L\right ]=\left (x+\frac{1}{2}\right )\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+\frac{3}{4}L,$

$\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}}dx=3\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1},\frac{11}{2}\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}}=\frac{11}{2}L.$

Adding the three parts:

$x\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+\left (\frac{1}{2}+3\right )\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+\left (\frac{3}{4}+\frac{11}{2}\right )L+C,$

so $α=\dfrac{7}{2}$ and $β=\dfrac{25}{4}$.

$α+2β=\frac{7}{2}+\frac{25}{2}=16$

Hence, the answer is 16.

text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation 

$2\cos x\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\sin 2x-4y\sin x,x\in \left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$. If $y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=0$, then $y^{'}\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )+y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Dividing $2\cos x\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\sin 2x-4y\sin x$ by $2\cos x$ and using $\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x$:

$\frac{dy}{dx}+2y\tan x=\sin x$

Since $\int 2\tan xdx=2\ln \sec x$, the integrating factor is

$\text{I.F.}=e^{2\ln \sec x}=\sec ^{2}x$

Multiplying through by $\sec ^{2}x$:

$y\sec ^{2}x=\int \sin x\sec ^{2}xdx=\int \sec x\tan xdx=\sec x+C$

$y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=0$ gives $0=\sec \frac{π}{3}+C=2+C$, so $C=-2$ and

$y=\cos x-2\cos ^{2}x$

Then $y^{'}=-\sin x+4\sin x\cos x$, and at $x=\frac{π}{4}$:

$y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-1,y^{'}\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+2$

$y^{'}\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )+y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=1$

Hence, the answer is 1.

text: Let $\mathrm{H}_{1}:\frac{x^{2}}{\mathrm{a}^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{\mathrm{b}^{2}}=1$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}:-\frac{x^{2}}{\mathrm{A}^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{\mathrm{B}^{2}}=1$ be two hyperbolas having length of latus rectums $15\sqrt{2}$ and $12\sqrt{5}$ respectively. Let their eccentricities be $e_{1}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{2}}$ and $e_{2}$ respectively. If the product of the lengths of their transverse axes is $100\sqrt{10}$, then $25\mathrm{e}_{2}^{2}$ is equal to $_________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{2b^{2}}{\mathrm{a}}=15\sqrt{2} \\ 1+\dfrac{\mathrm{b}^{2}}{\mathrm{a}^{2}}=\dfrac{5}{2} \\ \mathrm{a}=5\sqrt{2} \\ \mathrm{b}=5\sqrt{3} \\ \dfrac{2\mathrm{A}^{2}}{\mathrm{B}}=12\sqrt{5} \\ 2\mathrm{a}\cdot 2\mathrm{B}=100\sqrt{10} \\ 2.5\sqrt{2}.2\mathrm{B}=100\sqrt{10} \\ \mathrm{B}=5\sqrt{5} \\ \mathrm{A}=5\sqrt{6} \\ \mathrm{e}_{2}^{2}=1+\dfrac{\mathrm{A}^{2}}{\mathrm{B}^{2}} \\ =1+\dfrac{150}{125} \\ \mathrm{e}_{2}^{2}=1+\dfrac{30}{25} \\ 25\mathrm{e}_{2}^{2}=55 \end{array}$
